explanation: The crystal, a red square frame standing on one corner, carries no national or religious meaning. Its adoption let Israel's Magen David Adom join the movement in 2006.
learnMore: Emblems of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement

claims.text: The red crystal was adopted in 2005, by the Third Additional Protocol to the Geneva Conventions, as an additional protective emblem.
The red Star of David has not been adopted as a protective emblem under the Geneva Conventions, and the red lion and sun was recognized in 1929, long before 2005.
The red crystal is a red square frame set on one corner, with no national, political or religious meaning.
Magen David Adom of Israel was admitted to the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement in 2006.
